questions.stem: What is the defining characteristic of a NEON-inspired architecture?
options: Storage and compute are tightly bundled in one server
Storage is separated from compute so each can scale independently
All data is kept in memory
Every query runs on a single node
Data is stored only on the client device
questions.explanation: NEON-inspired architecture separates storage from compute, allowing systems to scale more efficiently and flexibly.

questions.stem: In traditional database systems, what happens when more processing power is needed?
options: Only the compute tier is scaled
Storage is automatically reduced
The entire system, including storage, often has to be scaled even if storage is sufficient
Nothing changes because compute is unlimited
Queries are moved to the client
questions.explanation: Because storage and compute are bundled, scaling processing power often means scaling the whole system, which creates cost and scalability inefficiencies.

questions.stem: Which well-known implementation applies serverless principles to PostgreSQL by separating compute nodes from storage layers?
options: Databricks
Hadoop
Kafka
Neon
Redshift
questions.explanation: Neon is named as a well-known implementation that separates compute from storage for PostgreSQL using serverless principles.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a core characteristic of a NEON-inspired architecture?
options: Shared storage that remains persistent and durable
Stateless or semi-stateless compute nodes that can start or stop quickly
A coordination layer that manages consistency and transaction integrity
Compute nodes that each hold their own private copy of all data
Multiple workloads operating on the same storage without duplicating data
questions.explanation: Because compute nodes are independent, multiple workloads share the same storage without duplicating data; private per-node copies would defeat the design.

questions.stem: In the school analogy from I Am Datapedia!, what do the library and the desks represent?
options: The library is compute; the desks are storage
The library is storage; the desks are compute
Both represent storage
Both represent compute
The library is the network; the desks are users
questions.explanation: The library where all books are stored represents storage, and the desks students borrow to read represent compute.

questions.stem: In the school analogy, what does adding more desks during exam season illustrate?
options: Compute can scale without building a new library (storage)
Storage must be duplicated for every new user
Books must be copied to each desk
The library must close during peak times
Compute and storage must grow together
questions.explanation: The school adds desks without building a new library, showing that compute scales independently while storage stays centralised.

questions.stem: Why does a NEON-inspired architecture enable cost efficiency?
options: Because storage is free
Because all data is compressed
Because it needs no coordination layer
Because it eliminates the need for backups
Because organisations only pay for compute when it is actively used
questions.explanation: Cost efficiency comes from paying for compute only while it is actively used, since compute instances can scale up or down with demand.

questions.stem: How does separating storage from compute improve reliability?
options: By storing every record twice on each node
By removing the need for transactions
By making compute nodes permanent
By running all queries in the browser
By managing storage durability independently from compute failures
questions.explanation: Storage durability is managed independently, so a compute failure does not threaten the durable storage layer.

questions.stem: How can development, testing and production environments benefit from a NEON-inspired design?
options: They can spin up separate compute instances pointing to the same underlying data layer
Each must copy the full dataset into its own storage
They must share a single compute node
Only production is allowed to access storage
They must run on-premises
questions.explanation: Separate compute instances can point to the same underlying data layer, improving agility without duplicating data.

questions.stem: With which broader architectural shift does NEON-inspired architecture align?
options: Monolithic, on-premises mainframe design
Tightly coupled single-server databases
Cloud-native, elastic and disaggregated system design
Paper-based record keeping
Client-only desktop applications
questions.explanation: NEON-inspired architecture reflects the broader move toward cloud-native, elastic and disaggregated design, aligning with lakehouse and distributed systems.
